pharm: Inhibits fungal cytochrome P450-dependent 14-alpha-lanosterol demethylation, blocking ergosterol synthesis in the fungal cell membrane.
quick: IV load 6 mg/kg q12h x2, then 4 mg/kg q12h; oral 200 mg q12h
Take oral 1 hour before or after food
Can cause fetal harm; use effective contraception
Avoid IV if CrCl <50 (cyclodextrin accumulates); oral preferred
LFTs, visual function, ECG/electrolytes, trough levels
summary: Voriconazole is a broad-spectrum triazole antifungal that is first-line therapy for invasive aspergillosis and is also used for candidemia, esophageal candidiasis, and serious Scedosporium and Fusarium infections. It has non-linear pharmacokinetics with wide interpatient variability driven by CYP2C19 polymorphism, so therapeutic drug monitoring is recommended. Key safety concerns include hepatotoxicity, QT prolongation, dose-related visual disturbances, photosensitivity with skin malignancy risk, and extensive CYP-mediated drug interactions.
indications: Candidemia in non-neutropenic patients and other deep-tissue Candida infections
Serious infections caused by Scedosporium apiospermum and Fusarium species, including Fusarium solani, in patients intolerant of or refractory to other therapy

dosage.d: Loading 6 mg/kg q12h for first 24 h, then maintenance 4 mg/kg q12h
Loading 6 mg/kg q12h for first 24 h, then 3-4 mg/kg q12h

dosage.n: Take 1 h before or after a meal

dosage.d: 200 mg q12h (>=40 kg); 100 mg q12h if <40 kg
dosage.n: Treat at least 14 days and 7 days after symptoms resolve

dosage.d: Standard loading dose, then halve the maintenance dose
Use oral route; avoid IV due to cyclodextrin (SBECD) accumulation
dosage.n: Monitor serum creatinine if IV used

admin: IV infuse over 1-2 hours at a maximum rate of 3 mg/kg/hr; do not bolus
Give oral tablets/suspension at least 1 hour before or 1 hour after a meal
Correct hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia, and hypocalcemia before and during therapy
Obtain trough levels for therapeutic drug monitoring (typically 1-5.5 mg/L)
Review all concomitant medications for CYP interactions before starting
moa: Voriconazole inhibits fungal cytochrome P450-mediated 14-alpha-sterol demethylase (CYP51), the enzyme that converts lanosterol to ergosterol. Depletion of ergosterol and accumulation of toxic methylated sterol precursors disrupt the integrity and function of the fungal cell membrane, producing a fungistatic effect against yeasts and fungicidal activity against many molds including Aspergillus.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to voriconazole or excipients
Coadministration with CYP3A4 substrates that can cause life-threatening QT prolongation (pimozide, quinidine, ivabradine, lurasidone)
Coadministration with sirolimus, rifabutin, eplerenone, naloxegol, tolvaptan, venetoclax (ramp-up in CLL/SLL), voclosporin
Coadministration with strong CYP enzyme inducers: rifampin, carbamazepine, long-acting barbiturates, St. John's wort, ritonavir 400 mg q12h, efavirenz >=400 mg/day
relative: Proarrhythmic conditions / congenital long QT / electrolyte disturbances
Galactose intolerance (oral suspension contains sucrose; tablets lactose)
monitor: Visual function if therapy exceeds 28 days
ECG and serum electrolytes (K, Mg, Ca)

preg: Voriconazole can cause fetal harm based on animal data (teratogenicity and embryotoxicity). Avoid in pregnancy unless the benefit clearly justifies the risk; advise females of reproductive potential to use effective contraception during therapy.
lact: It is not known whether voriconazole is excreted in human milk; because of the potential for serious adverse reactions in the breastfed infant, avoid breastfeeding or discontinue the drug.
renal: In moderate-to-severe renal impairment (CrCl <50 mL/min) the IV vehicle sulfobutyl ether beta-cyclodextrin (SBECD) accumulates; use the oral formulation and monitor serum creatinine if IV is unavoidable. No oral dose adjustment is needed for renal impairment.
hepatic: Use the standard loading dose but halve the maintenance dose in mild-to-moderate hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh A and B). Voriconazole has not been studied in severe (Child-Pugh C) impairment; monitor LFTs closely.

major: Strong CYP inducers (rifampin, carbamazepine, barbiturates, St. John's wort) - markedly reduce voriconazole levels (contraindicated)
Sirolimus, pimozide, quinidine, ergot alkaloids - increased toxic levels (contraindicated)
Tacrolimus / cyclosporine - voriconazole raises levels; reduce dose and monitor
Warfarin and other coumarins - increased prothrombin time; monitor INR
moderate: Statins (CYP3A4-metabolized) - increased levels and myopathy risk
Phenytoin - bidirectional; increase voriconazole dose and monitor phenytoin
Omeprazole / other CYP2C19 substrates - increased levels
Methadone - increased levels and QT risk
interactions.food: Take oral voriconazole at least 1 hour before or after a meal; high-fat meals reduce absorption.
interactions.diagnostics: Can elevate liver enzymes and prolong the QT interval on ECG.

rare: Skeletal fluorosis and periostitis with long-term use

monitoring: Liver function tests at baseline and during therapy
Serum electrolytes (potassium, magnesium, calcium) and ECG
Visual function if treatment exceeds 28 days
Renal function (serum creatinine) when IV used
Signs of skin malignancy with prolonged therapy
counsel: Visual changes such as blurred vision or altered color perception are common and usually reversible; do not drive at night during treatment
Avoid direct sunlight and use sun protection due to a risk of severe sunburn and long-term skin cancer
Take oral doses on an empty stomach, one hour before or after eating
Avoid alcohol and tell your doctor about all other medicines and herbal products
Report yellowing of the skin/eyes, dark urine, severe rash, or palpitations promptly
pk: Rapid (IV); steady state in ~5-6 days without loading
Variable, dose-dependent (non-linear kinetics); ~6 hours at usual doses
Tablets/powder store at 15-30 C; reconstituted suspension up to 14 days at 15-30 C
pearls: Boxed-warning-level safety: hepatotoxicity, QT prolongation, and visual disturbance dominate monitoring
Non-linear pharmacokinetics and CYP2C19 polymorphism cause wide level variability; use therapeutic drug monitoring (trough ~1-5.5 mg/L)
Avoid IV form if CrCl <50 due to cyclodextrin vehicle accumulation - switch to oral
Massive CYP2C19/2C9/3A4 interaction profile - always review concomitant drugs
missed: Take a missed oral dose as soon as remembered; if it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed one. Do not double up. For IV therapy, missed doses are managed by the treating team.
overdose: No specific antidote. Overdose may worsen photophobia and other dose-related effects; manage supportively with monitoring of vital signs and ECG. Voriconazole is hemodialyzable (clearance ~121 mL/min), and the cyclodextrin IV vehicle is also removed by hemodialysis.
